cards.text: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, has let Israel go (Exodus 13:17). Now the LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, to have the people turn back and camp by the sea near Pi-hahiroth. Turn BACK. Right by the sea.

cards.question: The LORD says Pharaoh will say something about the Israelites camped by the sea. What?

cards.text: Then God says He'll harden Pharaoh's heart so Pharaoh will chase them. And Israel does exactly what God said.

cards.question: God says He'll gain honor through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will ___ that He is the LORD.

cards.text: The king gets word that the people have fled. And Pharaoh and his officials change their minds.

cards.question: Pharaoh and his officials say, "What have we done?" What do they say they've done?

cards.text: Picture a boss who signs off on your two weeks' notice, then realizes nobody else knows how the copier works. Pharaoh gets his chariot ready, takes his army and picks out 600 of his best chariots.

cards.question: Pharaoh leaves every chariot in Egypt behind except his 600 best ones.

cards.text: The LORD hardens Pharaoh's heart, just like He said. Pharaoh chases Israel and catches up with them camped by the sea.

cards.question: The Israelites look up and see the Egyptians marching after them. What do they do?

answers.text: Cry out to the LORD in terror
Line up to fight the army

cards.text: Then they turn on Moses: "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die?" Whoo, they did NOT ease into that one.

cards.question: The people tell Moses it would have been better to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.

cards.text: Moses answers, "Do not be afraid." Friend, I held my breath every time somebody opened the junk drawer I was stuck in for years, and I think Moses is calmer than that with a whole ARMY coming.
Stand firm, he tells them, and they'll see the LORD's salvation, which He will accomplish for them today.

cards.question: Moses tells the people that the Egyptians they see today, they will never see again.
Moses says the LORD will ___ for them, and they need only to be ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses, "Tell the Israelites to go forward." Friend, forward is the SEA.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to lift up his staff. What is Moses to do with his hand?

answers.text: Stretch it out over the sea to divide it
Raise it toward the sky over Egypt
Lay it on the heads of the people

cards.question: God says the Israelites will go through the sea on ___ ground.

cards.text: God says He'll harden the Egyptians' hearts so they follow Israel right in, and they'll know that He is the LORD. Then the angel of God and the pillar of cloud, both going ahead of Israel's camp, start to move.

cards.question: The angel of God and the pillar of cloud move from in front of Israel's camp to behind it.

cards.text: The cloud stands between Egypt's camp and Israel's, there in the darkness, and it lights up the night. After all my years in a dark junk drawer, friend, I would've begged to camp next to that cloud.

cards.question: All night long, Egypt's army closes in on Israel's camp.

cards.text: Moses stretches out his hand over the sea. And all that night, the LORD drives the sea back.

cards.question: What does the LORD use to drive the sea back all night?

cards.text: The sea turns into dry land, and the waters are divided. Israel walks right through the sea.

cards.question: Israel walks through the sea on dry ground, between walls of water. Where are those walls?

answers.text: On their right and on their left
Ahead of them and behind them
Only on the side facing Egypt

cards.text: Friend, I flinch when one drop from the sink hits me, and these folks are walking between WALLS OF WATER. Then here come all Pharaoh's horses, chariots and horsemen, right into the sea after them.
At morning watch, the LORD looks down on Egypt's army from the pillar of fire and cloud. He throws their camp into confusion.

cards.question: The LORD causes the Egyptians' chariot ___ to wobble, so they have difficulty driving.
The Egyptians say the LORD is fighting for Israel against Egypt.

cards.text: Now even the Egyptians are saying what Moses told Israel. At the LORD's word, Moses stretches his hand over the sea again, and at daybreak the sea goes back to normal.

cards.question: As the Egyptians retreat, the waters flow back over the army that chased Israel into the sea. How many of them survive?

cards.text: But Israel walked through the sea on dry ground. That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians.

cards.question: Israel sees the great power the LORD used over the Egyptians. How do the people respond?

answers.text: They fear the LORD and believe in Him and Moses
They build an altar right there on the shore
They argue over who should lead them now

cards.text: Then Moses and the Israelites sing a song to the LORD. Friend, when I sing in the bakery, my oven timer goes off early just to get me to stop.

cards.question: The song opens, "I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted." Then it says what the LORD has done. What?

answers.text: Thrown horse and rider into the sea
Split the rock in the wilderness
Sent frogs over the land of Egypt

cards.text: Then the song gets personal. It calls the LORD "my God" and "my father's God."

cards.question: Back at the sea, Moses promised the people they'd see the LORD's salvation. Now the song says the LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my ___.

cards.text: The LORD is a warrior, the song says, and He cast Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea. The finest of his officers drowned in the Red Sea, and the depths covered them as they sank like a stone.

cards.question: Now the song talks straight to God. What does it say has shattered the enemy?

cards.text: The song keeps going. God overthrew His adversaries by His great majesty, and His burning wrath consumed them like stubble.

cards.question: Then the song looks back at the currents standing firm like a wall. What does it say piled the waters up?

answers.text: The blast of the LORD's nostrils
The stamp of the LORD's feet

cards.text: Then the song tells what the enemy declared: "I will pursue, I will overtake." That's a whole to-do list, friend, and I can't even get through "I will clean the oven."

cards.question: Then the song answers all that bragging: God blew with His breath, and the ___ covered them.
The song asks, "Who among the gods is like You, O LORD?" Its point is that some gods are just as great as He is.

cards.text: The song says the earth swallowed the enemy up. Then it looks ahead, to where God is taking His people.

cards.question: With loving devotion, the song says, God will lead the people He redeemed. Where will He guide them?

cards.text: Then the song says the nations will hear about all this, and it names some of them: Philistia, Edom, Moab and Canaan.

cards.question: The song says that when the nations hear what God did, they will tremble.

cards.text: Terror and dread will fall on them, and they'll be as still as a stone until God's people pass by. And God will bring His people in and plant them on the mountain of His inheritance.

cards.question: The song ends by saying the LORD will ___ forever and ever.

cards.text: Then Miriam the prophetess takes a tambourine in her hand. She's the sister of Aaron, Moses's brother.

cards.question: Miriam starts to play. Who follows her with tambourines and dancing?

cards.text: And Miriam sings back to them, "Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted…" Friend, I'm stuck to a gold base, and even I want to grab a tambourine and dance.
